project_name: JSE Money Market ISIN Issuance Service
initial_requirements: The JSE Securities Exchange South Africa needs an electronic service for issuing identifiers for dematerialized money-market instruments. Money Market Forum participants should be able to submit requests through STRATE to create, amend, or delete ISIN codes, with the JSE returning identifiers quickly enough to support same-day trading, clearing, and settlement. The service should reduce manual processing while preserving controlled and reliable market records.

messages.content:
Hello, I’m GPTREI, your requirements elicitation assistant. I’ll be gathering detailed information about the JSE Money Market ISIN Issuance Service to understand the needs, workflows, and constraints clearly.

Before we begin, are my assumptions about the scope aligned with yours, or do you expect this interview to focus on something different?

Yes, that sounds aligned. We’re mainly looking at the electronic process for issuing, amending, and deleting ISINs for dematerialized money-market instruments through STRATE, with the JSE responding quickly enough to support same-day market activity. The main aim is to reduce manual handling while keeping the records controlled, accurate, and reliable.
Thank you. To start off, could you please introduce yourself and your connection to this project?

I’m speaking as part of the JSE side of the market services and reference data function, where we’re responsible for the issuance and maintenance of these money-market identifiers. My connection to the project is that I help represent the business needs around accuracy, turnaround time, and controlled processing for the ISIN service.
Thanks, that helps. Could you describe the current process or system you use today for creating, amending, and deleting these money-market ISINs?

Today, a lot of it is still handled manually or with semi-manual coordination between the participant, STRATE, and the JSE team. Requests are typically checked, validated, and then processed by staff, which can slow things down and creates a bit of operational dependence on people being available. That’s part of why we want a proper electronic service, so the workflow is cleaner and faster.
What current processes do you want to change or improve, or what features do you hope to get from this project?

The biggest improvement is to remove the manual back-and-forth and make the request and response flow electronic end to end. We also want quicker turnaround, ideally fast enough to support same-day issuance or changes when the market needs it. On top of that, we want better control and traceability so the records stay consistent and auditable.

So far, I have these main features or goals: electronic end-to-end request and response flow, faster turnaround for same-day activity, and stronger control and traceability for auditable records. Are there any other features you would like to see in this project?

Yes, we’d also want proper validation so bad or incomplete requests are rejected early with clear feedback. It would be useful to have status tracking or acknowledgements so participants know whether a request is received, being processed, or completed. And from our side, some form of reporting or enquiry capability would help us monitor activity and resolve issues more easily.
Based on your description, do you think role-based access and approval control should also be included, so only authorised participants can submit or act on requests?

Yes, definitely. This is a controlled market service, so only authorised participants should be able to submit requests, and any internal action on our side should also be restricted to the right users. Approval control is important too, especially for amendments and deletions, because we need to make sure those changes are properly authorised before they go through.

So the main features/functions I’ve captured are: electronic end-to-end request handling, fast turnaround for same-day market activity, strong control and traceability, validation with clear rejection feedback, status tracking/acknowledgements, reporting/enquiry capability, role-based access, and approval control for sensitive changes. Are there any other features you would like to add before we prioritise them?

One more important thing is audit history, so we can see who did what and when for every request and change. It would also help if the service kept a clear reference or transaction number that participants can use when following up. Beyond that, I think the list is in the right area for prioritising.
Thank you. Which three of these features are the highest priority for the first release?

For the first release, I’d prioritise the electronic end-to-end request handling, the fast turnaround for same-day activity, and the validation with clear rejection feedback. Those are the core things needed to get the service working reliably and reduce the operational pain straight away.
Please elaborate on what you want the electronic end-to-end request handling to accomplish.

It should let authorised participants submit create, amend, and delete requests electronically through the normal channel, and then let us process and return the outcome without manual rekeying. The request should carry all the necessary data in a structured way, so it can move through validation, approval, and issuance cleanly. Ideally it also gives the participant a clear response or reference back so they know the request has been dealt with.
Could you describe more about what data a create, amend, or delete request must include so it can be validated and processed correctly?

For a create request, we’d need enough information to uniquely identify the instrument and support the ISIN issue, so the instrument details, issuer details, maturity date, and any market-specific identifiers we use internally. For an amend or delete request, the existing ISIN or reference number is essential, plus the specific fields to change or the reason for the deletion if that’s required by process. I’m not completely sure yet which fields are mandatory versus optional, so that would need to be confirmed with the operations team and the participants’ data standards.
Understood. Could you describe the fast turnaround requirement in more detail, such as what same-day means in practice and when the service must return a response?

Same-day means the request should be processed and returned while the market is still active, so participants can use the identifier for trading, clearing, or settlement on that day if everything is in order. In practice, we’d want a response as quickly as possible after submission, ideally within minutes for straightforward requests, but I don’t have an exact service-level target yet. For anything that needs manual review or approval, it should still be completed in time to avoid disrupting the day’s processing.
Please elaborate on what you want the validation with clear rejection feedback to accomplish.

The system should check the request before it goes any further, so obvious issues like missing fields, invalid formats, duplicate requests, or an attempt to change something that can’t be changed are caught early. If a request is rejected, the participant should get a clear reason and enough detail to correct and resubmit it without having to chase us manually. We’d want the rejection to be specific and consistent, not just a generic failure message.
Are there any other stakeholders you think have valuable insights into this project, whose needs should be considered, and why?

Yes, definitely STRATE is one of the key ones because they operate the submission channel and need the workflow to fit their operational controls. The Money Market Forum participants are also important because they are the actual users submitting and tracking requests, and the JSE operations and compliance teams need to be considered because they’re responsible for approvals, records, and market integrity. I’d also include settlement and clearing stakeholders, since the identifiers have to work cleanly for downstream same-day processing.
What would you consider a successful deployment of this service?

A successful deployment would be one where participants can submit requests electronically without disruption, and the JSE can issue or update identifiers reliably and quickly enough for same-day market use. It would also mean we’ve reduced manual handling, improved consistency in the records, and there are no major operational issues after go-live. If the users trust the process and the responses are clear and timely, I’d consider that a good outcome.

To summarize, we discussed an electronic end-to-end ISIN issuance service via STRATE for dematerialized money-market instruments, supporting create/amend/delete requests, fast same-day turnaround, validation with clear rejection feedback, traceability, access and approval control, audit history, transaction references, and reporting/enquiry needs. Success would mean reliable electronic submission, reduced manual handling, timely responses, and trusted, accurate records.

Is there anything else you would like to add?

Only that we should keep the process simple for participants but still controlled enough for the JSE and STRATE to manage risk. It would also help if the service can support exceptions and corrections cleanly, because in a live market there will always be cases that don’t fit the normal path. Beyond that, I think the summary covers the main needs well.
